title: Monday rebalance: repair hard caps and refresh momentum sleeve
observation: Equity AAPL+MSFT+NVDA is 30.53% of equity NAV (cap 30%). Crypto cash is 19.57% of crypto NAV (min 20% / max invested 80%), so invested is 80.43%. Equity live P&L since 2026-09-20 book is +0.391% vs SPY +0.646% over the same short window. Crypto live P&L is +2.178% vs BTC +4.543%. Screen still ranks MSFT/META/XLE/AAPL/XLV/AMZN/JPM/NVDA as the equity top cohort; XLF ranks 10th and drops out of the 8-name target. Crypto screen ranks AVAX/LINK/SOL/ETH ahead of BTC.
logic: Options considered: (1) hold all positions until more history accumulates; (2) trim only the hard-cap breaches (equity tech to 30%, crypto cash back to 20%) and leave the rest; (3) full weekly momentum rebalance to allocate.py targets, which also brings tech under 30% (~29.2%) and restores crypto cash near 20% while rotating XLF->AMZN and BTC->SOL. Chose (3) as the Monday proposal because caps are already breached, the locked tech rule explicitly waits for this weekly pass, and the screen still supports the momentum cohort. Did not propose a method switch: one day of live marks is not enough evidence.
why: Respect locked caps without waiting for a larger breach, and keep the book aligned with the current 63d momentum signal Jordan already approved.
how_to_judge: Over the next four Monday marks: (a) equity tech sleeve stays <=30% NAV; (b) crypto cash stays >=20%; (c) equity vs SPY and crypto vs BTC total return and max drawdown versus a no-rebalance counterfactual if we keep a simple hold log.
